atoms.name: Divide, conquer, combine
atoms.one_line: Split into sub-problems, solve them, merge the answers; cost satisfies T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n).

atoms.name: Solving recurrences
atoms.one_line: Master theorem, recursion trees and substitution (including sqrt(n) splits) turn T(n) into a bound.

atoms.name: Merge sort and quicksort costs
atoms.one_line: Merging m and n items takes m+n-1 comparisons; merge sort is n log n; first-pivot quicksort on sorted input is n(n-1)/2.

atoms.name: Maximum and minimum
atoms.one_line: Pairing elements finds both in ceil(3n/2)-2 comparisons; second largest by tournament n+ceil(log n)-2.

atoms.name: Inversions and maximum subarray
atoms.one_line: Merge sort counts inversions in n log n; the best subarray lies left, right or across the midpoint.

atoms.name: Strassen and fast multiplication
atoms.one_line: Seven half-size products instead of eight give n^(log2 7); Karatsuba uses three products.

atoms.name: Closest pair and search-style splits
atoms.one_line: Closest pair is n log n with a linear strip check; binary-search style splits discard half.
